root_cause.text: The cleanup loop in `setup_nic_devices()` uses `while(i--)` which decrements the index `i` before executing the loop body, causing the device at the failing index (the one that triggered the error jump) to be skipped and its resources leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The current cleanup loop while(i--) skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak." The patch changes `while(i--)` to `do { ... } while(i--)` to ensure the failing index is processed.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The cleanup loop in `setup_nic_devices()` uses `while(i--)` which decrements the index `i` before executing the loop body, causing the device at the failing index (the one that triggered the error jump) to be skipped and its resources leaked.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states: "The current cleanup loop while(i--) skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak." The patch changes `while(i--)` to `do { ... } while(i--)` to ensure the failing index is processed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error cleanup loop to also destroy the NIC device at the index that failed to initialize.
intent_record.what: Changed the loop construct from a while loop (`while (i--)`) to a do-while loop (`do { ... } while (i--);`) in the error cleanup path of `setup_nic_devices`.
intent_record.how: The loop now executes its body at least once even when `i` is zero, whereas previously it would skip the body entirely if `i` was zero. This ensures that the device at the current index `i` (the one that failed setup) is also destroyed, not just the previously created devices (indices 0 to i-1).

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the cleanup loop to include the device at the failing index, preventing the resource leak caused by the while(i--) decrementing before execution.
